nodes.text: Mind the dust — that's not dirt, that's *product*. Garton. Forty years at this wheel, boy and man, and the pond hasn't missed a day's work yet, which is more than I can say for anyone else in this town.

choices.text: What's your quarrel with the ferry bell?
Forty years — the town must have changed.

nodes.text: Quarrel! It's not a *quarrel*, it's a position. The bell rings on a west wind whether there's a soul at the crossing or not, and it scares my herons off the shallows. I've raised it at the moot. Twice. But mind — the boy checks my mooring lines every morning like it's nothing, so the bell and I have settled into a working hatred. Don't you go fixing it.

Changed? When I started, the Round was mud, the bank was a toll box, and Silverfall silver came through four caravans a season. Then the mountain sealed its cellar and the caravans thinned and this town learnt to feed itself — fields, pond, orchard. Now the cellar's open again and everybody's dreaming of silver. *Flour*, I tell them. Empires run on flour.
Flour by the sack, wheat by the sheaf, and a loaf if the morning batch behaved.
Passing's free. The gossip's ground fine here too — cheaper than Dunna's and twice as reliable.
